hero.title: What dog should we get? The quiz to take as a couple
hero.description: Do you want a dog but can't agree on which one? You each answer 12 questions and the quiz tells you which dog would suit your couple best. There's a photo for every result!
hero.subtitle: 12 questions • 3 minutes each • on one phone

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.p1: This quiz is a game to play as a couple. It helps you find the dog that would fit your life, whether that's a golden retriever or a rescue dog. It asks 12 very simple questions. For example, it asks where you live and how long the dog would be left alone.
section1.p2: Take the question about the dog's size. You can choose between “small, it fits on your lap”, “medium, you can still carry it”, “big, a proper dog” and “huge, almost a pony”. If you answer “small”, the quiz gives points to small dogs like the dachshund. If your partner answers “huge”, it gives points to the Bernese mountain dog. At the end, the quiz adds up your answers and keeps the dog with the most points.
section1.p3: The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. Then the quiz shows you your dog as a couple, with its photo. It also shows the dog each of you would have got alone and the questions where you gave different answers. That's often where the conversation starts!
section1.p4: You can also take the quiz on your own and answer for your couple. But it's more fun to find out what your partner answered.

section2.title: The 12 dogs in the quiz
section2.intro: The quiz can give 12 results. There are ten well-known breeds and the rescue dog. There's also a result for couples who aren't ready for a dog yet. Here's who each dog suits best.

section3.title: Choosing a dog as a couple: what to ask yourselves
section3.intro: A dog lives between ten and fifteen years, so it's a decision you make together. Before you go and see one, there are four subjects it's better to agree on.
section3.sub1Title: Who's going to look after it?
section3.sub1Text: This is the question that causes the most arguments. A dog has to go out three times a day, even on a rainy Sunday morning. Before you adopt, agree on who does what at home. For example: who walks it in the morning and who takes it to the vet.
section3.sub2Text: A big sporty dog will be unhappy in a studio. A very clingy little dog will be unhappy too if it's alone ten hours a day. Look at your life as it is today and not as you'd like it to be. And if you don't agree yet on where you want to live, start there, because a garden changes a lot of things.
section3.sub3Text: A dog costs more than people think. On top of the food, there's the vet and someone to look after it when you go on holiday without it. Some breeds also need regular grooming. A big dog costs more than a small one, simply because it eats more. The best thing is to do the sums together before you adopt.
section3.sub4Title: A puppy or an adult dog?
section3.sub4Text: A puppy is very cute, but it needs months of training and it will wake you up at night. An adult dog is often already house-trained and you already know its character. In a shelter you'll find dogs of all ages, and even pedigree dogs. If you'd rather go to a breeder, go and see the puppy's parents and the place where it grew up.

section4.title: What if you don't agree?
section4.p1: It's not a big deal, and it happens to a lot of couples! If one of you dreams of a husky and the other wants a dog that fits in a bag, look at the list of your different answers. You'll see what you disagree on, for example the dog's size or how long it would be alone. Most of the time, you're only stuck on two or three questions.
section4.p2: Lots of couples get a dog before having a child. The two are very different of course, but it already shows how you get organised when someone depends on you.
section4.p3: And if one of you doesn't want a dog at all, don't push. It's better to wait until each of you wants one, otherwise the same person will always end up looking after it.

section5.title: What you should know about this quiz
section5.p1: This quiz is a game. The descriptions give the most common character of each breed, but every dog is different and its training matters as much as its breed. Before you choose, go and see breeders or shelters and spend time with the dog.
section5.p2: Your answers aren't saved, they stay on your phone. We only count which dog you get, to see which results come up most. Your name isn't saved either. The photos of the dogs were created for this page.

seo.faq1A: The quiz can give 12 results. There are ten breeds: the golden retriever, the corgi, the French bulldog, the Cavalier King Charles spaniel, the Australian shepherd, the dachshund, the poodle, the Shiba Inu, the Siberian husky and the Bernese mountain dog. There's also the rescue dog and “a plush dog, for now” for couples who aren't ready yet.
seo.faq2Q: How is the result worked out?
seo.faq2A: Each answer gives points to the dogs that match it. For example, if you answer that you live “in a city apartment, with no outdoor space”, the French bulldog and the Cavalier King Charles spaniel get points but the husky doesn't. When you take the quiz together, it adds up your answers and the dog with the most points becomes your dog as a couple.
seo.faq3Q: Can you take the quiz on your own?
seo.faq3A: Yes. Just choose “On my own, for our couple” and answer with your couple in mind. You'll get a dog but you won't be able to compare your answers.
seo.faq4Q: What dog for a young couple in an apartment?
seo.faq4A: It mostly depends on how much time you have. In an apartment, it's better to have a dog that doesn't need to run for hours. That's the case for the French bulldog, the Cavalier King Charles spaniel, the dachshund and the poodle. The Shiba Inu also works if you're at work part of the day. On the other hand, an Australian shepherd or a husky needs space and a lot of exercise.
seo.faq5Q: How do we know if we're ready for a dog?
seo.faq5A: The quiz has a result for that: “a plush dog, for now”. It comes up when the dog would be alone all day or when you travel a lot. It also comes up when one of you wants a dog more than the other. If you get it, look after a friend's dog for a weekend to see how it goes.
seo.faq6A: No. Your answers stay on your phone. We only count which dog you get, to see which results come up most, and your name isn't saved.
